title: The elderly
hook: Francis called grandparents the memory of a people
tomorrow: who is lonely, just one phone call away from you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the poor: Lazarus at the gate, the one Jesus named. By name. Today, the people who remember everyone's name, and the street before it changed.

Somebody's grandmother remembers what the corner store sold before it was a phone shop, the song everyone danced to at her wedding, and which cousin was named for whom. So what do grandparents carry that nobody else can? Pope Francis gave it a name. He called grandparents the memory of a people. Not a museum, but a living memory, the kind that only works if someone younger sits down and asks.
screen: `BEFORE IT WAS A PHONE SHOP.` → `WHAT DO GRANDPARENTS CARRY?` → `THE MEMORY OF A PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Scripture puts the old at the center. In Leviticus, the command is physical, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "Rise up before the hoary head, and honour the person of the aged man." Stand up when they come in. The prophet Joel pictures a day when God's spirit is poured out on everyone, and gives the old and the young two different jobs: "your old men shall dream dreams, and your young men shall see visions." Francis took up that pairing in his letter to young people. The old dream, he said, and the young take those dreams and turn them into vision. Neither works alone. The Church even honors a pair of grandparents. Tradition, not the Gospels, names Mary's parents Joachim and Anne, and Catholics keep their feast together, the grandparents of Jesus. In Luke, the ones in the Temple who recognize the child are two old ones, Simeon and Anna, who had waited and watched. Francis warned against a throwaway culture that treats the old as finished. In this tradition, they hold the stories that tell a family, a parish, a street who it is. Lose them unheard, and the people forgets itself. That's why a visit to an old person isn't only charity. It's how memory gets passed on.
screen: `RISE UP BEFORE THE HOARY HEAD.` · `OLD MEN DREAM, YOUNG MEN SEE.` · `JOACHIM AND ANNE.` · `NOT A THROWAWAY.` · then, large: `THE MEMORY OF A PEOPLE.`

segments.voice: Find one thing an older person gave you or left you: a photo, a ring, a recipe card, a rosary, a voice message. Hold it, or picture it, and look at it closely for the sit. What story comes with it that only they could tell? Think of one older person you could visit or call this week, and one question you'd like to ask them.
The elderly. The people who carry what a family remembers, and dream the dreams the young turn into vision. Today's word.
Your line: the memory of a people. It lives only while someone asks. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics celebrate Saints Joachim and Anne, by tradition Jesus's grandparents, and the Church now keeps a World Day for Grandparents and the Elderly; parishes bring Communion to elderly people who can't come to Mass.
